q: What air ratio or flue gas oxygen should my furnace or boiler run at?
title: Air ratio targets for furnaces and boilers
short: Air ratio is 21 divided by (21 minus the percent oxygen in flue gas). BEE's MSME guidelines target 1.15 to 1.20 for oil-fired and 1.12 to 1.15 for gas-fired furnaces. For boilers the targets are 1.32 to 1.38 on coal and 1.32 to 1.39 on biomass, with carbon monoxide kept within 200 ppm.
audience: Boiler operators and furnace in-charges with a flue gas analyser

ul: Forging, heat treatment and glass furnaces: 1.15 to 1.20 on liquid fuel, 1.12 to 1.15 on natural gas
Aluminium pit furnace: 1.32 to 1.38 on coal, 1.15 to 1.20 on furnace oil
Galvanizing and lead bath furnaces: 1.18 to 1.24 on liquid fuel

sections.h: Boilers, thermic fluid heaters and hot air generators
ul: Biomass such as wood, bagasse and rice husk: standard 1.49 to 1.56, target 1.32 to 1.39
Liquid fuel: standard 1.26 to 1.33, target 1.18 to 1.24
Natural gas: standard 1.15 to 1.18, target 1.12 to 1.15

sections.h: Turning it into an oxygen reading
p: Rearranged, oxygen % = 21 minus 21 divided by the air ratio. An air ratio of 1.15 is about 2.7% oxygen, 1.20 is 3.5% and 1.38 is about 5.8%. Read oxygen and carbon monoxide together: low oxygen with carbon monoxide above 200 ppm means too little air.

ul: Use an online or portable oxygen analyser and adjust air to the reading.
Fit automatic air to fuel ratio control on the burner.
Size the blower correctly and place it close to the burner.
Seal openings so cold air does not leak in.

senseible: Senseible turns fuel invoices into monthly fuel use and emissions, so a combustion tune-up shows up as less fuel for the same output.

sources.label: BEE, Energy Conservation Guidelines for MSME Sector (2019): Tables 6.8, 6.22, 6.39, 6.66 and 6.71, with the air ratio formula
